query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A meaningful grouping axis for duration variance; categories match short_description well (WiFi->connectivity, VPN->connectivity, database->database). Partly overlaps original 'category' column but the derived values from text appear sound.

per_column.name: primary_system_affected
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis from category; different systems plausibly have different resolution times. Values are well-grounded in the short_description (VPN->vpn, WiFi->wifi_network, database->database).

per_column.name: assigned_to_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician workload/skill is a genuine driver of duration. But values contradict source: row1 closed_by 'Charlie Whitherspoon' yet assigned beth_anglin; row5 closed_by 'Luke Wilson' yet charlie_whitherspoon. Appears to duplicate/misalign existing assigned_to; produced values not consistently grounded.

per_column.name: ticket_handoff_occurred
per_column.rationale: Handoffs plausibly increase duration, a useful signal. However the table gives no clear evidence of handoffs in the sampled rows; the boolean appears asserted without support from the source text (only assigned_to/closed_by pairs available, not exposed here).

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity/impact type is a strong candidate driver for duration. Mappings are mostly defensible (cannot connect/access->access_restricted, printing->service_unavailable), a warranted categorisation of the description.

per_column.name: time_of_day_opened
per_column.rationale: Directly derivable from opened_at timestamp and could explain duration (off-hours staffing). Buckets match samples exactly. Somewhat derivable from an existing column but adds a usable grouping axis.

per_column.name: scope_impact
per_column.rationale: Blast radius is a strong duration driver. Grounding is weak: 'single_user' for connectivity/VPN is defensible, but scope is largely inferred and not explicitly stated in short_description; some assignments are speculative.

per_column.name: caller_profile
per_column.rationale: Essentially a restatement of caller_id with little new leverage for duration. Values also appear misaligned/invented relative to available source (caller not shown in samples, yet specific names asserted).

per_column.name: recurring_issue_indicator
per_column.rationale: Recurrence could plausibly affect duration and is a useful axis. But nothing in the sampled source text supports a true/false recurrence determination; the boolean appears asserted without grounding.

judge.rationale: Most columns supply genuine, distinct axes (category, affected system, severity, scope, time-of-day, handoff, recurrence) that could plausibly explain duration variance, so analytical usefulness is solid overall. caller_profile is weak (redundant with caller_id). Groundedness is mixed: text-derivable columns (incident_category, primary_system_affected, issue_severity_signal, time_of_day_opened) are well supported, but assigned_to_technician contradicts closed_by in samples, and ticket_handoff_occurred, recurring_issue_indicator, caller_profile, and partly scope_impact assert specifics the sampled source text does not warrant, indicating hallucination.
